source.citation: Thompson, D'Arcy W. (1917) On Growth and Form. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. Chapter XII, 'The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera', pp. 587-611, Figs. 308-317.
source.page_to_leaf: IA page-image index n = printed page + 19 (verified: n611 = p. 592)
source.claim_text: Foraminiferal shells are generated by chambers added in logarithmic-spiral succession with (near-)constant growth ratios, and the genera form a continuous geometric series transformable into one another.

E1_logarithmic_spiral.source_locus: Ch. XI p. 493ff (general spiral), Ch. XII p. 597 'according to our equation r = e^{theta cot alpha}'

variables.r: radius vector from the pole (proloculus centre)
variables.alpha: constant angle between tangent and radius vector

E2_whorl_ratio_from_constant_angle.formula: W = r(theta + 2 pi) / r(theta) = exp(2 pi cot(alpha));  half-whorl ratio rho_half = exp(pi cot(alpha)) = sqrt(W)
E2_whorl_ratio_from_constant_angle.source_locus: p. 593: 'ratio of 1.5 between the breadths of successive whorls corresponds (table on p. 534) to a constant angle of about 86 degrees'; von Moller's half-whorl log-difference 0.088 = log 1.225 and whole-whorl 0.176 = log 1.5

E3_chamber_geometric_succession.formula: L_{n+1} / L_n = rho (constant);  L_n = L_1 * rho^(n-1);  log L_n linear in n
E3_chamber_geometric_succession.source_locus: p. 595: van Iterson Triloculina rotunda rho = (319/34)^(1/8) = 1.323; Rhumbler Pulvinulina menardii rho ~ 1.187; p. 593 von Moller Fusulina W ~ 1.5 per whorl

variables.L_n: linear dimension (breadth) of chamber or whorl n

E4_volume_ratio_from_mass_proportional_g.formula: V_1 = q V_0;  V_n = q (V_0 + ... + V_{n-1})  =>  V_{n+1}/V_n = 1 + q  (constant);  rho = (1+q)^(1/3) for similar chambers

variables.q: growth increment as a fraction of the whole pre-existing mass

E5_equal_angle_condition.formula: chamber n occupies vectorial angle theta_n = n * delta_theta (constant delta_theta); 180 deg (Biloculina), 120 deg (Triloculina), ~20 deg (Cyclammina, Fig. 313); delta_theta -> 0 with alpha -> 90 deg gives the Nodosarian straight limit; alpha = 90 deg gives the Orbitolitid circular limit

E6_generative_chamber_model_used_in_scri.formula: centre_n = r_0 rho^n (cos(n dtheta), sin(n dtheta)) + (0, 0, T n);  chamber radius a_n = a_0 rho^n;  rho = exp(dtheta cot alpha)
E6_generative_chamber_model_used_in_scri.note: Thompson's verbal model (similar chambers, continued proportion, constant subtended angle, optional screw translation T for Textularia p. 605) made explicit; it is the Raup (1966) W-D-T family restricted to discrete similar chambers.

rho.meaning: linear ratio between successive chambers (or half-whorls)
rho.regime: 1.05 - 1.6 (Thompson: 1.187 Pulvinulina, 1.225 Fusulina half-whorl, 1.26 Przibram's cube-root-of-2 'rule', 1.323 Triloculina, 1.5 Fusulina whorl)

delta_theta_deg.meaning: vectorial angle subtended by one chamber

alpha_deg.meaning: constant angle of the equiangular spiral

overlap.meaning: fraction of chamber radius embraced by its successor (Globigerina small, Cyclammina/Pulvinulina large)

T.meaning: screw translation per chamber perpendicular to the spiral plane (Textularia, Globigerina helicoid)

state_variables_and_parameters.boundary_conditions: Initial chamber (proloculus) approximately spherical, radius a_0; Naumann's cyclocentric conchospiral needed only for radii, not for whorl breadths (p. 594 footnote).

rhumbler_pulvinulina_menardii.note: 'not strictly constant from chamber to chamber, but subject to a small secondary fluctuation'

przibram_1913_rule.note: cube root of 2 (volume doubling); Thompson: 'Neither rule seems to me to be well grounded'

empirical_biological_claims.claim: Successive whorls/chambers of spiral foraminifera are in continued (geometric) proportion, i.e. log size is linear in chamber/whorl number.
empirical_biological_claims.testable_with: Dryad fusulinid half-whorl series; CV whorl radii from the fusulinid thin section

empirical_biological_claims.claim: The ratio is only approximately constant: a 'small secondary fluctuation' exists (Rhumbler), and Thompson warns 'we must not exaggerate the regularity or constancy' (p. 605).
empirical_biological_claims.testable_with: CV of successive ratios; trend of ratio vs stage

empirical_biological_claims.claim: Fusulina whorls grow by about 1.5 per whorl (1.225 per half-whorl), constant angle ~86 degrees.
The genera differ only in numerical coefficients (ratio, subtended angle, overlap, translation) and pass into one another by small continuous gradations; classification is 'artificial'.
empirical_biological_claims.testable_with: continuity of per-specimen (rho, allometry) across five fusulinid genera; generative model morphospace

empirical_biological_claims.claim: Growth ratio is a consequence of growth proportional to the existing mass with similar chambers.
empirical_biological_claims.testable_with: Lean theorem (algebraic); not empirically tested here

dataset.name: Data from: Heterochronic origin of spherical fusulinid foraminifera in the Late Paleozoic
dataset.primary_article: Shi Y. (2021) Heterochronic origin of spherical fusulinid foraminifera in the late Paleozoic. Paleobiology 47(1): 115-133 (Crossref-verified; single author).
dataset.structure: 1396 outlines, each 'Outline <NAME>-<k>' or '<k>-<NAME>' followed by 40 lines of x y pixel coordinates; k = whorl-growing stage (half-whorl, alternating sides of the axial section); 106 specimens, 5 genera (prefix letter T/P/S/Z/R).
dataset.match_to_claim: Taxon class (fusulinid foraminifera, as in Thompson's von Moller exemplar) and variable (breadth of successive half-whorls, 180 degrees apart) both match; whorl-level not chamber-level.
